label: Thomas Aquinas, Summa theologiae I q.16… supports If one thing is more noble than another, it…
note: ST I q.16 a.3 co. states that each thing is knowable in so far as it has being and that 'sicut bonum convertitur cum ente, ita et verum'. The premise reads convertibility for the comparative: whatever is more noble than another is also more good and more true than it. The passage states convertibility of the terms with being and a proportion of knowability to being; it does not mention nobility or state that the comparatives coincide.
